q.en: What is the deadline, and what happens when it arrives?
q.es: ¿Cuál es la fecha límite y qué pasa cuando llega?

claims.en: Public Law 119-103, the law now in force, makes its money available, unless that law or the applicable fiscal 2027 spending law provides otherwise, until “whichever of the following first occurs”: a later law appropriating money for a project or activity it covers, the applicable fiscal 2027 spending law if enacted without any provision for that project or activity, or “December 11, 2026.”
claims.es: La Ley Pública 119-103, la ley vigente, deja disponibles sus fondos, salvo que esa ley o la ley de gasto aplicable del año fiscal 2027 disponga otra cosa, hasta «lo primero que ocurra» de lo siguiente: una ley posterior que asigne fondos a un proyecto o actividad que ella cubre, la ley de gasto aplicable del año fiscal 2027 si se promulga sin ninguna disposición para ese proyecto o actividad, o el «11 de diciembre de 2026».

cites.quote: Unless otherwise provided for in this Act or in the applicable appropriations Act for fiscal year 2027
shall be available until whichever of the following first occurs
The enactment into law of an appropriation for any project or activity provided for in this Act.
The enactment into law of the applicable appropriations Act for fiscal year 2027 without any provision for such project or activity.
December 11, 2026.

claims.en: Section 111(b) of that law says “obligations for mandatory payments due on or about the first day of any month,” if that month begins after October 2026 and no later than 30 days after December 11, 2026, “may continue to be made.”
claims.es: La sección 111(b) de esa ley dice que «las obligaciones de pagos obligatorios que vencen el primer día de cualquier mes o alrededor de esa fecha», si ese mes empieza después de octubre de 2026 y a más tardar 30 días después del 11 de diciembre de 2026, «pueden seguir haciéndose».

cites.quote: Notwithstanding section 106, obligations for mandatory payments due on or about the first day of any month that begins after October 2026 but not later than 30 days after the date specified in section 106(3) may continue to be made
December 11, 2026.

claims.en: A Congressional Research Service report, last updated December 10, 2018, says that if funding does not resume in time, “under the Antideficiency Act, an agency must cease operations, except in certain situations when law authorizes continued activity.”
claims.es: Un informe del Servicio de Investigación del Congreso, actualizado por última vez el 10 de diciembre de 2018, dice que si los fondos no se reanudan a tiempo, «según la Ley Antideficiencia, una agencia debe cesar sus operaciones, salvo en ciertas situaciones en que la ley autoriza que la actividad continúe».

cites.quote: under the Antideficiency Act, an agency must cease operations, except in certain situations when law authorizes continued activity.
Updated December 10, 2018

q.en: If funding lapses, what keeps running and what pauses?
q.es: Si se acaba el financiamiento, ¿qué sigue funcionando y qué se suspende?

claims.en: The Congressional Research Service, in a report updated December 10, 2018, says that in a shutdown an agency may obligate some funds in certain “excepted” areas, but “these obligations are highly restricted,” and it “must shut down nonexcepted activities.”
claims.es: El Servicio de Investigación del Congreso, en un informe actualizado el 10 de diciembre de 2018, dice que durante un cierre una agencia puede comprometer algunos fondos en ciertas áreas «exceptuadas», pero «estas obligaciones están muy restringidas», y «debe suspender las actividades no exceptuadas».

cites.quote: the agency may obligate some funds in certain “excepted” areas, but these obligations are highly restricted.
the agency must shut down nonexcepted activities
Updated December 10, 2018
In a shutdown situation, Congress and the President have not enacted interim or full-year appropriations for an agency

claims.en: Federal law (31 U.S.C. 1342) bars accepting unpaid work or employing people beyond what the law authorizes “except for emergencies involving the safety of human life or the protection of property,” and those emergencies do not include “ongoing, regular functions of government” whose suspension would not imminently threaten life or property.
claims.es: La ley federal (31 U.S.C. 1342) prohíbe aceptar trabajo no remunerado o emplear personal por encima de lo que autoriza la ley «salvo en emergencias que afecten la seguridad de la vida humana o la protección de la propiedad», y esas emergencias no incluyen «las funciones ordinarias y regulares del gobierno» cuya suspensión no amenazaría de forma inminente la vida ni la propiedad.

cites.quote: may not accept voluntary services for either government or employ personal services exceeding that authorized by law except for emergencies involving the safety of human life or the protection of property.
ongoing, regular functions of government the suspension of which would not imminently threaten the safety of human life or the protection of property.

claims.en: The same report says programs funded outside yearly spending laws, “such as entitlements like Social Security and other mandatory spending,” “also may be affected by a funding gap, if program execution relies on activities that receive annually appropriated funding.”
claims.es: El mismo informe dice que los programas financiados fuera de leyes anuales de gasto, «como los programas de prestaciones, por ejemplo el Seguro Social, y otros gastos obligatorios», «también pueden verse afectados por una interrupción de fondos si su ejecución depende de actividades que reciben fondos asignados cada año».

cites.quote: such as entitlements like Social Security and other mandatory spending—also may be affected by a funding gap, if program execution relies on activities that receive annually appropriated funding.

claims.en: We did not retrieve agencies' own plans for a lapse, so this answer does not say which programs at any one agency keep running.
claims.es: No consultamos los planes de cada agencia para una interrupción de fondos, así que esta respuesta no dice qué programas de una agencia concreta siguen funcionando.

claims.en: Under the Constitution, a bill that has “passed the House of Representatives and the Senate” is “presented to the President,” who signs or returns it with objections; a returned bill becomes law only if “two thirds” of each chamber agree to pass it again.
claims.es: Según la Constitución, un proyecto «aprobado por la Cámara de Representantes y el Senado» se «presenta al Presidente», que lo firma o lo devuelve con sus objeciones; un proyecto devuelto solo se convierte en ley si «dos tercios» de cada cámara vuelven a aprobarlo.

cites.quote: Every Bill which shall have passed the House of Representatives and the Senate, shall, before it become a Law, be presented to the President of the United States; If he approve he shall sign it, but if not he shall return it, with his Objections
If after such Reconsideration two thirds of that House shall agree to pass the Bill

claims.en: For H.R. 6500, the law now in force, the Senate passed the House’s bill “with an amendment” on August 8, 2026, and it went to the president only after the House voted on September 1 to “agree to the Senate amendments.”
claims.es: En el caso de la H.R. 6500, la ley vigente, el Senado aprobó el proyecto de la Cámara «con una enmienda» el 8 de agosto de 2026, y se envió al presidente solo después de que la Cámara votó el 1 de septiembre para «aceptar las enmiendas del Senado».

q.en: How much does it authorize, and for what?

claims.en: A Congressional Research Service primer, updated December 4, 2025, says the National Defense Authorization Act “provides authorization of appropriations for the Department of Defense (DOD), nuclear weapons programs of the Department of Energy, and other defense-related activities” and that, “Unlike an appropriations bill, the NDAA does not provide budget authority for government activities.”
claims.es: Una guía del Servicio de Investigación del Congreso, actualizada el 4 de diciembre de 2025, dice que la Ley de Autorización de Defensa Nacional «autoriza asignaciones para el Departamento de Defensa (DOD), los programas de armas nucleares del Departamento de Energía y otras actividades relacionadas con la defensa» y que, «a diferencia de un proyecto de asignaciones, la NDAA no otorga autoridad presupuestaria para las actividades del gobierno».

cites.quote: The National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) provides authorization of appropriations for the Department of Defense (DOD), nuclear weapons programs of the Department of Energy, and other defense-related activities.
Unlike an appropriations bill, the NDAA does not provide budget authority for government activities.
Updated December 4, 2025

claims.en: For H.R. 8800 as the House Armed Services Committee reported it on June 15, 2026, the committee’s report recommends “an overall discretionary authorization for national defense programs of $1.15 trillion for fiscal year 2027” and says the bill authorizes $1.14 trillion for programs within the committee’s jurisdiction.
claims.es: Para la H.R. 8800 tal como la presentó la Comisión de Servicios Armados de la Cámara el 15 de junio de 2026, el informe de la comisión recomienda «una autorización discrecional total para los programas de defensa nacional de 1,15 billones de dólares para el año fiscal 2027» y dice que el proyecto autoriza 1,14 billones de dólares para los programas bajo la jurisdicción de la comisión.

cites.quote: June 15, 2026.--Committed to the Committee of the Whole House on the State of the Union and ordered to be printed

The committee recommends an overall discretionary authorization for national defense programs of $1.15 trillion for fiscal year 2027 and authorizes $1.14 trillion for fiscal year for programs within its jurisdiction.
The bill authorizes $1.14 trillion of discretionary funding to support national defense requirements.

claims.en: For S. 4784 as the Senate Armed Services Committee reported it on June 15, 2026, that committee’s report “recommends an overall discretionary authorization of $1,140.1 billion in fiscal year 2027, including $1,099.0 billion for base DOD programs, $41.1 billion for national security programs in the DOE, and $11.9 billion for defense-related activities outside the jurisdiction of the NDAA.”

claims.en: A Congressional Research Service primer, updated December 4, 2025, says reaching a final Senate vote may require “one or more cloture processes (by which three-fifths of the Senate, typically 60 Senators, votes to limit consideration),” and that “The Constitution requires that the House and Senate approve the same bill in precisely the same form before it is presented to the President,” so a change by either chamber needs the other’s agreement.
claims.es: Una guía del Servicio de Investigación del Congreso, actualizada el 4 de diciembre de 2025, dice que para llegar a una votación final en el Senado pueden hacer falta «uno o más procesos de cierre del debate (en los que tres quintos del Senado, por lo general 60 senadores, votan para limitar la consideración)», y que «la Constitución exige que la Cámara y el Senado aprueben el mismo proyecto exactamente en la misma forma antes de presentarlo al Presidente», así que un cambio de cualquiera de las dos cámaras necesita el acuerdo de la otra.

claims.en: Under the Constitution, the President then signs the bill or returns it with objections; a returned bill becomes law only if “two thirds” of each chamber agree to pass it again, and one not returned “within ten Days (Sundays excepted)” becomes law unless Congress’s adjournment prevents its return.
claims.es: Según la Constitución, el Presidente luego firma el proyecto o lo devuelve con sus objeciones; un proyecto devuelto solo se convierte en ley si «dos tercios» de cada cámara vuelven a aprobarlo, y uno que no se devuelve «dentro de diez días (sin contar los domingos)» se convierte en ley, salvo que el aplazamiento del Congreso impida su devolución.

cites.quote: If he approve he shall sign it, but if not he shall return it, with his Objections to that House in which it shall have originated
If after such Reconsideration two thirds of that House shall agree to pass the Bill

If any Bill shall not be returned by the President within ten Days (Sundays excepted) after it shall have been presented to him, the Same shall be a Law, in like Manner as if he had signed it, unless the Congress by their Adjournment prevent its Return, in which Case it shall not be a Law.

claims.en: Both measures are bills: the House committee’s report calls H.R. 8800 “the bill (H.R. 8800),” and S. 4784 is “An original bill to authorize appropriations for fiscal year 2027,” so either one, once both chambers pass it in the same form, would be presented to the President.
